title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 — deferred supply, phenology and fulfillment status
purpose: Separate different ways the expedition repaired temporary inaccessibility instead of collapsing them into generic 'later supply'.

cases.taxon_or_material: Crinum bulb plus earlier seed packet from C. R. Orcutt
cases.problem: Rudolf could not wait in California for the flowering time of all useful plants.
cases.repair_strategy: delegated later supply through a local botanical supplier
observed_status_chain: large Crinum bulb sent later and received by Rudolf in Cambridge
Rudolf proposes a larger standing arrangement for seeds and bulbs of plants whose flowering he could not wait for
cases.open: onward forwarding to Hosterwitz, survival, cultivation, flowering, drawing and model use not yet closed

cases.problem: Flowering season of most conifers in central California had already passed; direct observation failed.
cases.repair_strategy: planned later local supply through botanical acquaintances
observed_status_chain: local botanist network expected to send flowers later

cases.problem: Desired habitat trip near Shasta was time- and cost-intensive; Goodale's delayed telegram ultimately instructed them not to go.
cases.repair_strategy: route rejection followed by cultivated institutional substitution
observed_status_chain: flowering cultivated plant encountered at St Louis botanical garden
cases.open: exact genealogy from St Louis reference to Corning drawing 133264 and Harvard model 444 remains open

status_ontology: entered observable target state (for example flowering)

repair_types.definition: wait for a later biological state and ask a local contact to send material
later material actually reaches the expedition/museum relay after the traveller has left the field site
replace a costly habitat visit with cultivated access that provides the desired observable state

main_result: Phenological failure was not a terminal category. The network could shift time, supplier, route or site of observation. These repairs had different fulfillment statuses and should be tracked event by event.
analytical_claim: Transport could move future observability rather than a completed observation. Seeds and bulbs carried the capacity for a later biological state; deferred fresh material carried a future moment of flowering; cultivated institutions could substitute a currently observable specimen for an abandoned habitat route.
negative_evidence_rule: A plan to send material later is not evidence that the material was ever dispatched or received. Keep promised/requested, dispatched, received, survived, flowered and modelled as separate statuses.
next_retrievals: Search Goodale/Harvard correspondence for receipt and forwarding of the May 4 live cactus/bulb box and June Orcutt material.
Search Hosterwitz letters July 1892 onward for Crinum, Orcutt, California bulbs/seeds, germination, flowering or loss.
Search later 1892-1894 correspondence for Sequoia flowering material sent by California botanists or Lemmon-related contacts.
Crosswalk any fulfilled deferred supply against Corning preparatory drawings and model labels.
Keep Darlingtonia substitution separate from deferred supply because its access problem was repaired by changing site rather than waiting for later delivery.
map_decision: Represent repair status as asynchronous packet/event edges or status cards. Do not add hypothetical geographic lines for promised-but-unverified later supply.
